'''Ivan Aničin''' (born 25 March 1944 in [[Bor, Serbia|Bor]], Serbia, [[Yugoslavia]], died 2 April 2016) was a  [[Yugoslavia|Yugoslav]] and [[Serbs|Serbian]] [[nuclear physicist]], [[particle physicist]], [[astrophysicist]], and [[Physical cosmology|cosmologist]], university [[Full Professor]] and Distinguished (teaching/research) Professor of scientific institutes in [[Belgrade]] ([[Serbia]]), [[Bristol]] (United Kingdom), [[Grenoble]] (France), and [[Munich]] (Germany).

He has been Head of Department of Nuclear and Particle Physics at [[University of Belgrade]] and [[Chair (Polish academic department)|Chief of Chair]] of Nuclear and Particle physics at Faculty of Physics, University of Belgrade, since 1997, and Director of Doctoral Studies in Nuclear and Particle Physics at University of Belgrade. Professor Aničin was distinguished professor of both Institute of Physics Belgrade<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ipb.ac.rs/ |title=Home |website=ipb.ac.rs}}</ref> and [[Vinča Nuclear Institute|Vinča Institute for Nuclear Sciences]], where he led projects in [[cosmology]] and [[astroparticle physics]].

Aničin was member of several international projects, including [[LHC]] [[CERN]], ILIAS,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www-ilias.cea.fr/ |title=Archived copy |access-date=14 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161023183552/http://www-ilias.cea.fr/ |archive-date=23 October 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> [[Allchar deposit|LOREX]], and projects funded by the Serbian Ministry of Science and Technology.

==Education==
[[File:Aničin - Wolfendale - Puzović - LLL (Low Level Laboratory) - Low Background Level Radiation Laboratory - Cosmic Ray Lab - Institute of Physics Belgrade.jpg|thumb|right|Professor Aničin with [[Arnold Wolfendale|Sir Arnold Whittaker Wolfendale]] [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]], British astronomer who served as [[Astronomer Royal]], and professor Jovan Puzović ([[CERN]] and Faculty of Physics, [[University of Belgrade]]).]]
Ivan Aničin was educated in [[Yugoslavia]] ([[Belgrade]]), United Kingdom ([[Bristol]]), France ([[Grenoble]]), and Germany ([[Munich]]).

He completed elementary school and Gymnasium education in Belgrade. At [[University of Belgrade]] he attained a First Class degree in physics in 1967, completed his [[Magister (degree)|Magister of Sciences in Physics or PhD degree in Physics]] in 1970, and [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Sciences in Physics]] degree in 1973.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110812181825/http://bmw.ff.bg.ac.rs/Katedre/KatFizJez/IvanAnicin.PDF Biography of professor dr sci. physics Ivan Aničin.]Old version of Faculty of Physics of University of Belgrade website, last updated 2003 by Faculty of Physics of University of Belgrade web-admin. Source: http://www.ff.bg.ac.rs. 2011-02-17. URL:http://bmw.ff.bg.ac.rs/Katedre/KatFizJez/IvanAnicin.PDF. Accessed: 2011-02-17. (Archived by WebCite® at https://www.webcitation.org/5wZ1BrUGM?url=http://bmw.ff.bg.ac.rs/Katedre/KatFizJez/IvanAnicin.PDF {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110812181825/http://bmw.ff.bg.ac.rs/Katedre/KatFizJez/IvanAnicin.PDF |date=12 August 2011 }}) Permalink.</ref><ref name="autogenerated2003">[http://bmw.ff.bg.ac.rs/Katedre/KatFizJez/IvanAnicin.PDF Biography of professor Ivan Aničin; old version of Faculty website, last updated 2003] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110812181825/http://bmw.ff.bg.ac.rs/Katedre/KatFizJez/IvanAnicin.PDF |date=12 August 2011 }} (14 February 2010)</ref>

Aničin did his postdoctoral studies, research, and, for some time, teaching, in the United Kingdom at [[University of Bristol]], in [[Grenoble]], France, at [[Institut National de Physique Nucléaire et de Physique des Particules|the Institut National de Physique Nucléaire et de Physique des Particules (IN2P3)]] of [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|the National Center of Scientific Research (Centre national de la recherche scientifique, or CNRS)]], [[European Synchrotron Radiation Facility|the European Synchrotron Radiation Facility (ESRF)]], and [[Institut Laue–Langevin|the Institut Laue-Langevin, or ILL]], in [[Munich]], Germany, at [[Max Planck Institute for Physics]], and in Yugoslavia, at [[Vinča Nuclear Institute|the Institute for Nuclear Sciences "Boris Kidrič" (later renamed to INS "Vinča")]].

==Scientific career==
Ivan Aničin earned [[Magister (degree)|Magister of Sciences in Physics or PhD degree in Physics]] in 1970, and [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Sciences in Physics]] degree in 1973., in the field of nuclear physics.<ref name="autogenerated2003"/> His interests and research are in the fields of nuclear spectroscopy of [[gamma radiation]] and conversion electrons and their angle correlations, studies of rare and low probability nuclear and fundamental processes (especially [[neutrinoless double beta decay]], non-resonant excitations), [[Neutrino detector|detection of solar neutrinos]], detection of [[dark matter]], measurements of cosmic radiation, and methodology of experimental nuclear physics in general.<ref name="autogenerated2003"/><ref>[http://147.91.68.190/Engleski/CurriculumDoctoralPhysics.htm DOCTORAL STUDIES OF PHYSICS (14 February 2010)]</ref>

==Teaching career==
[[File:Prof. dr Ivan Aničin i prof. dr Đuro Krmpotić - Nuclear Physicists - Institute for Nuclear Sciences Vinča and Faculty of Physics University of Belgrade.jpg|thumb|right|Ivan Aničin with his student-days professor of Nuclear Physics and a colleague from [[Vinča Nuclear Institute|Institute for Nuclear Sciences Vinča]] and Faculty of Physics [[University of Belgrade]], Đuro Krmpotić, during a filming on formerly top-secret nuclear projects in [[Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia]].]]
During and after holding post-doctoral research positions in the United Kingdom, France, Germany, and [[Yugoslavia]], Aničin mostly taught at [[University of Belgrade|Belgrade University]] and the [[University of Novi Sad]], at [[Vinča Nuclear Institute|the Institute for Nuclear Sciences "Boris Kidrič" (later renamed to INS "Vinča")]][http://www.vinca.rs]), and Institute of Physics Zemun (renamed to "Institute of Physics Belgrade")[http://www.ipb.ac.rs].

Aničin started his teaching career at 1969, as assistant professor for Nuclear Physics and for General Courses in Physics, at University of Novi Sad. He also taught two more subjects at University of Novi Sad: Methods of Measurements, and Data Treatment.

At University of Belgrade, professor Aničin teaches or had taught the following subjects: Data Treatment in Physics, Order of Magnitude Physics, various courses of Nuclear Physics, Nuclear and Elementary Particle Physics, Foundations of Nuclear and Particle Physics, Higher Course in Nuclear Physics, Nuclear Instrumentation, Nuclear Spectroscopy, Selected Chapters of High Energy Physics, Detectors, Nondestructive Analysis, Rare Subatomic Processes, Astroparticle Physics, Radiation Physics.<ref name="autogenerated2003"/><ref>[http://147.91.68.190/Engleski/CurriculumDoctoralPhysics.htm DOCTORAL STUDIES OF PHYSICS] (14 February 2010)</ref><ref>[http://147.91.68.190/Engleski/CurriculumMaster_B.html Master Studies – THEORETICAL AND EXPERIMENTAL PHYSICS] (14 February 2010)</ref><ref>[http://147.91.68.190/Engleski/CurriculumMaster_A.html Master Studies – GENERAL PHYSICS] (14 February 2010)</ref>

From 1990 Aničin teaches [[History of physics|History of Physics]] and Philosophy of Physics at postgraduate Center for Multidisciplinary Studies at University of Belgrade.<ref name="autogenerated2003"/> From 1980 Aničin teaches specialized courses in "School of Isotopes" in [[Vinča Nuclear Institute|the Institute for Nuclear Sciences "Vinča"]][http://www.vinca.rs]).<ref name="autogenerated2003"/> In Belgrade Aničin also taught general courses in physics at the Faculty for Teachers (Pedagogical Academy).<ref name="autogenerated2003"/>

Professor Aničin is a frequent lecturer at Kolarac Institute,<ref>[http://www.astronomija.co.rs/predavanja/3383-lhc-prve-dve-godine.html Lecture entitled "Dark Matter and LHC", at Kolarac Institute] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110426021900/http://astronomija.co.rs/predavanja/3383-lhc-prve-dve-godine.html |date=26 April 2011 }}, "LHC – first two years" series of lectures. Source: Astronomy Magazine. Accessed: 2011-02-23.</ref><ref>Lecture entitled "Mysterious neutrino", at Kolarac Institute, "Mysteries and riddles of micro-world" series of lectures ("Mysterious neutrino", "In search of a missing particle", "Supersymmetry: reality, or illusion?"). {{cite web|url=http://www.astronomija.co.rs/predavanja/3383-lhc-prve-dve-godine.html |title=LHC - PRVE DVE GODINE &#124; Astronomski Magazin |accessdate=2011-02-23 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110426021900/http://astronomija.co.rs/predavanja/3383-lhc-prve-dve-godine.html |archivedate=26 April 2011 }}. Accessed: 2011-02-23.</ref> where he gives public lectures for a broader (non-physicists) audience.

Professor Aničin is author and lecturer of courses "How to teach physics – order of magnitude physics", "How to teach physics – nuclear and particle physics", and "How to teach physics – astrophysics and cosmology", at [[University of Belgrade]], aimed at college, high school, and elementary school professors and teachers, who need to advance their knowledge both in named fields on physics and in methodology and didactics, and at scientists and engineers at physics teaching positions. The courses are part of broader [[Master of Science]] level at Faculty of Physics, [[University of Belgrade]].<ref>[http://www.ff.bg.ac.rs Postgraduate education: Physics and Engineering Education, academic discipline "M.Sc. in Physics and Engineering" with professional title "Professor of Physics, Science, and Engineering – Master", awarded jointly by Faculty of Physics and University of Belgrade]</ref> These MSc courses are for teachers, professors, engineers, and graduated physicists only. They are part of postgraduate education scheme "Physics and Engineering Education for Graduated Physicists, Graduated Engineers, College Teachers, and Professors" academic discipline "MSc in Physics and Engineering" with professional title "Professor of Physics, Science, Informatics, and Engineering – Master", awarded jointly by Faculty of Physics and University of Belgrade. This diploma allows its holders to teach in any of the following subject areas, at college, high school, or elementary school level: physics, science, informatics and related subjects (e.g. computer programming languages), engineering, and mathematics.

Professor Aničin mentored or was member of degree granting committee of more than 200 [[Magister (degree)|MSc]], PhD, and [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Sciences in Physics]] degrees to American, British, Croatian, French, German, Greek, Iraqi, Iranian, Libyan, Montenegrin, Russian, Serbian, Slovenian, Soviet, and Yugoslavian physicists. He also mentored [[Magister (degree)|MSc]] and [[Doctor of Sciences|Doctor of Sciences in Physics]] degrees of his colleagues and successors at Faculty of Physics of University of Belgrade: professors Jovan Puzović (at [[CERN]] from 2000), and professor Goran Škoro (from 2004 on leave at UK [[Neutrino Factory]]).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.hep.shef.ac.uk/contact.php |title=Dept of Physics and Astronomy, University of Sheffield, Particle Physics and Particle Astrophysics: Group Directory |access-date=23 February 2011 |archive-date=20 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320174759/http://www.hep.shef.ac.uk/contact.php |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://hepunx.rl.ac.uk/uknf/ |title=UK Neutrino Factory homepage |access-date=23 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050325102847/http://hepunx.rl.ac.uk/uknf/ |archive-date=25 March 2005 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.hep.shef.ac.uk/research/uknf.php |title=About UK Neutrino Factory |access-date=23 February 2011 |archive-date=20 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120320174814/http://www.hep.shef.ac.uk/research/uknf.php |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Articles===
Aničin was a regular contributor to science journals and popular science magazines.
